phase: Accounting Empirical Recovery / F5 Phase B — Bilateral Component and Issuer-Applicability Audit

structural_F52_scope.interpretation: F52 issuer applicability removes false missingness for H/C/G/BNR columns but does not solve total F5 because F51 remains missing bilaterally.

scientific_interpretation: The F52 issuer-scope rule is empirically useful and methodologically distinct from missing-to-zero: 24 in-boundary cells per measure are structural non-issuer cases.
Seven applicable F52 bilateral cells per measure are directly/exactly recovered, covering H/C/G holdings of resident/foreign funds and rest-of-world holdings of resident fund shares.
F51 equity remains unavailable in every tested bilateral cell. Therefore total F5 cannot be reconstructed for any in-boundary cell, including those where F52 is structurally zero.
The next exact decomposition is F51 = F511 listed shares + F512 unlisted shares + F519 other equity. It must be tested bilaterally before aggregate-rank-only fallback.
No structural issuer simplification is applied to F511/F512/F519 in this phase; their issuer applicability is more heterogeneous than F52.

next_gate.name: F5 Phase C — bilateral F51 subcomponent bridge
required_checks: probe F511/F512/F519 separately in both W2 orientations and W1 external orientations using canonical _Z._Z dimensions
derive bilateral F51 only when all three subcomponents are resolved or a separately justified structural applicability rule is established
combine derived F51 with the Phase B F52 evidence/issuer scope to derive total F5 candidates
reconcile any recovered F51/F5 rows, columns and external partitions to published W0/W1 controls
if material bilateral coverage emerges, compute exact rank/nullity before materialization
if F51 subcomponents are also unavailable bilaterally, proceed to aggregate rank and freeze rather than allocate
